limitations: Direct controller timing, not HTTP/production throughput; short128-token fixtures do not establish general or long-context performance.
Three repeats per candidate, same fixture outputs, rotated order. Best depth is workload-specific; no automatic production depth change.
CUDA-event intervals include stream launch/idle/wait time and are not pure kernel time. Host command/apply ranges nest.
Kernel sums can overlap across streams; per-device kernel union is reported separately. NCCL kernel duration can include waiting for peers and is not pure wire time.
Traces cover only three warm decode rounds at depth4. Profiling changes timings; none of those timings select speed winners.
Family registration, packaged serving, packed batching, broader API and long-context quality gates remain incomplete.

findings.primary_target: Original BF16 dense projections: tune memory layout/tiles while retaining weights and qualifying arithmetic/output parity.
interpretation: Dense projections dominate compute in both short traces. Sampling host time mostly waits for earlier target/head GPU work; CUDA event intervals isolate this from sampling execution.
Ranks4/5 perform less shared-expert dense work and spend longer in NCCL than ranks0..3. These traces support a rank-imbalance hypothesis, not a measurement of pure network transfer time.
Keep depth4 as the reference. Depth6 gains only about2.7% on this prose fixture and does not lead on code; deeper drafting alone is not a large general improvement.
